## Summary of findings

**CRITICAL — Authentication bypass via JKU injection** (`src/oauth/token.js`, `src/oauth/jwks.js`)
`verifyExternalToken` trusts the attacker-controlled JWT `jku` header to fetch the verification key. The unused `src/http/safe-jwks.js` shows the correct, hardcoded approach.

`validateRedirect` uses `redirectUri.startsWith(client.baseUrl)`, bypassable via `https://portal.example.test.evil.com/cb` or `https://portal.example.test@evil.com/cb`. This lets an attacker receive OAuth codes/credentials meant for the legitimate client. An exact-match helper (`exact-redirect.js`) exists but is not used.

`byId` returns `undefined` for unknown clients; `validateRedirect` then throws a `TypeError` reading `.baseUrl`, instead of cleanly denying.
